issues.legal_issue: A compromise decree resolving an eviction suit created a licence rather than a lease where its terms and context showed no intention to establish a landlord-and-tenant relationship.
material_facts: The property owner had brought an action to evict the occupant, and the parties then entered into a compromise decree allowing the occupant to remain for a specified period.
The decree described payments for continued occupation as rent and required a deposit to be adjusted against the final period of occupation.
If the occupant failed to pay for three consecutive months, the owner could execute the existing decree to evict the occupant before the specified period ended.
The compromise was reached after the owner had lost at trial and during the appeal.
issues.conclusion: The compromise decree created a licence, not a lease, because the parties did not intend to create a landlord-and-tenant relationship.
issues.legal_principle: The decisive test for distinguishing a lease from a licence is the parties’ intention, determined from the substance of the agreement and all relevant circumstances. Exclusive possession is not conclusive; an interest in the property may indicate a lease, while circumstances showing that the parties did not intend a legal landlord-and-tenant relationship may indicate a licence. The use of the word “rent” or payment for occupation is not decisive because rent may also describe payment by a licensee. The Court relied on Associated Hotels of India Ltd. v. R. N. Kapur, M. N. Clubwala v. Fida Hussain Saheb, State of Punjab v. British India Corporation Ltd., Issac v. Hotel De Paris, and approved Sumatibai Waman Kirlikar v. A. B. Shirgaonkar.

predicates.eviction_suit_resolved_by_compromise_dec: The property owner initiated proceedings to recover the property, and the parties resolved those proceedings by a compromise decree.
predicates.continued_occupation_permitted: The compromise decree allowed the occupant to remain in the property for a period after the settlement.
predicates.existing_decree_executable_to_evict_on_p: The decree allowed the owner to use that same decree to evict the occupant if the occupant defaulted on payments for continued occupation.
predicates.prior_eviction_action_indicates_no_new_t: The owner had sought to evict the occupant before the compromise, and the circumstances of that action indicated no intention to create a new tenancy.

issues.definition: When an eviction action is resolved by a compromise decree permitting continued occupation, and the decree or the surrounding circumstances show that the owner did not intend to establish a new tenancy, the occupation is a licence rather than a lease.

issues.legal_issue: An occupant permitted to remain under a compromise decree that created a licence was not entitled to tenant protection under the applicable house-rent control law.
material_facts: The compromise decree did not create a lease, but permitted the occupant to remain in the property subject to its terms.
The owner sought to execute the decree, and the occupant objected to execution while claiming protection as a tenant.
The applicable statutory definition included certain people against whom an eviction suit was pending but excluded a person against whom a decree or order for eviction had been made.
issues.conclusion: The occupant was not a tenant entitled to protection against eviction under the Act, and the eviction decree could be executed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(5) of the Orissa House-Rent Control Act, 1958 defined “tenant” to include a person against whom an eviction suit was pending, but not a person against whom a court had made a decree or order for eviction. Since the compromise decree created no lease and was an eviction decree, the occupant did not qualify for the claimed statutory protection.

predicates.execution_objection_to_eviction_decree: The occupant objected to execution of a court decree for eviction.
predicates.occupancy_is_a_licence_not_a_lease: The agreement permitting occupation created a licence rather than a landlord-and-tenant relationship.
predicates.eviction_decree_has_been_made: A court had made a decree or order for eviction against the occupant.

issues.definition: When an occupant objects to execution of an eviction decree, the occupation is a licence rather than a lease, and an eviction decree has been made, the occupant is not entitled to tenant protection.
